newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Elf rises in New York trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Elf rises in New York trade.

text.p: Shares in French energy company Elf Aquitaine rose on Tuesday boosted by a recommendation on the stock.

Elf rose 2-1/4 to 48-5/8 in active trade to highlight the market in foreign shares and American Depositary Receipts. The rise came after Merrill Lynch recommended the shares and called the company a "bull stock" for 1997.
"Its been exceptionally strong today," a trader said of Elf.

Among other European shares, Franco-Italian semiconductor maker SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV rose 3-1/8 to 69 after the company's chairman told London's Financial Times newspaper it would continue to outperform the market.

Nordic telecoms Nokia Group and LM Ericsson moved higher, pulled along by increases in high-tech stocks International Business Machines Corp and Motorola Inc. Nokia was up 1-7/8 to 64-1/2 and Ericsson rose 5/8 to 32-7/8.
Gulf Canada Resources Ltd rose 3/4 to 9 after it dismissed the latest defense of British bid target Clyde Petroleum Plc, saying the company's net assets were valued on unrealistic assumptions.
Gulf Canada was among the most active foreign shares in New York, with 1.1 million shares traded by early afternoon.

Latin American shares were mostly stronger, boosted by a firmer U.S. long bond. Brazilian bellwether Telebras was up 1-3/8 to 86-3/4, helped by brightening prospects for congressional passage of a constitutional amendment that would allow presidential re-election.
Advancers led decliners 346 to 197 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 43.8 million shares.
